newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent shuffles sideways under $18.52 resistance.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent shuffles sideways under $18.52 resistance.

text.p: IPE Brent shuffled sideways on Friday morning after earlier edging tentatively up from Thursday's close.
The July contract was up 13 cents a barrel at $18.45 at 1106 GMT after failing to hit an upside target of $18.52.
The market is "technically still vulnerable and the next downside targets...are $18.20 (Brent) and $19.60 (WTI)," commented Leslie Nicholas of brokers GNI in London.
"$18.52/55 is a notable resistance area. There may be some consolidation but this down move is not over yet, we believe," he added in a market report.
Dealers said that if Brent failed to climb above $18.52, the mid-point of Thursday's trading range, it was likely to move sideways at least until NYMEX pit trading resumes later on Friday.
Charles Gray at Prudential Bache in London saw a possible sideways range of $18.25 which was Thursday's low to $18.52 a barrel.

A mildly supportive report from the International Energy Agency (IEA) did little to help the market. The IEA reported accelerating oil demand growth next year and increased its forecast for the demand for OPEC oil later this year.
"It's not as bearish as some people were expecting," said a broker.
The IEA revised downwards its estimate of non-OPEC oil supply in the fourth quarter this year, leaving more room for OPEC oil.
Meanwhile, the physical market for crude oil remains weak with only gasoline in the United States likely to lend the wider oil market any support.
With refineries running flat out in the U.S., traders in Europe saw little chance of sending large quantities across the Atlantic.
IPE gas oil was up $1 a tonne at $166.75 at 1106 GMT having briefly dipped below $166 support on Thursday.
Dealers said demand in the key German market remains sluggish and saw a prompt overhang building up in the Mediterranean.
Barges in Rotterdam talked around 75 cents a tonne over the screen.
